title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Car Guy. Tip #1
body: Read the plate before you read the man. Anyone can be sitting in a Mercedes. Not everyone has three of the same digit, a low number, or a series that makes other drivers behave differently. He knows what his plate says about him and so does every other driver on Heydar Aliyev prospekti. It's a sealed deal if he's ever been pulled over and the conversation ended in under forty seconds.
caption:
Tip #1 😭 read the plate, not the badge.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Car Guy. Tip #2
body: Ask what he thinks of the Prius and watch the whole personality arrive. It is the most common car in this city, it is mostly taxis, and every car guy in Baku has a prepared speech about it that he is desperate to deliver. Let him. The speech is the content. It's a sealed deal if he owns one, defends it on fuel economy, and is still slightly embarrassed.
caption:
Tip #2 😭 read the plate, not the badge.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Car Guy. Tip #3
body: Check where the car came from. Bought here, or imported through Georgia, which is what half the interesting cars did, and he knows the customs number to the manat. Electric is the newest flex because of the exemption, and there is now a Tesla in this city on every third corner. It's a sealed deal if he can tell you the total landed cost of a car he doesn't own, for fun.
caption:
Tip #3 😭 read the plate, not the badge.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Car Guy. Tip #4
body: Watch the tint. It is too dark, it is always too dark, and he knows exactly which roads have cameras and which do not. There is a running negotiation between him and the state that has lasted years and both sides accept the terms. It's a sealed deal if he has a second, legal set of anything in the boot for exactly one week a year.
caption:
Tip #4 😭 read the plate, not the badge.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Car Guy. Tip #5
body: Ask about the car wash. It's not maintenance, it's a ritual, weekly minimum, and there is one specific place with one specific man who does it properly and he will not switch. The car is cleaner than the flat. It's a sealed deal if it has rained within an hour of a wash and he genuinely took it personally.
caption:
Tip #5 😭 read the plate, not the badge.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Car Guy. Tip #6
body: Ask what's in the speakers and how loud. Windows down on the Boulevard road at midnight is the whole point of owning it. Russian rap, Turkish, or something local, and the volume is the message. He is not going anywhere. He is driving. It's a sealed deal if he has a specific loop through the city that he drives when he's thinking, and it takes forty minutes, and he does it alone.
caption:
Tip #6 😭 read the plate, not the badge.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Car Guy. Tip #7
body: Look at what's parked at his father's house. That's the real garage, and that's where the Land Cruiser lives. The son drives the loud one, the father drives the quiet one, and the quiet one costs four times as much. If he laughs when you ask about his dad's car, you've found the money. It's a sealed deal if the father's car is fifteen years old, immaculate, and worth more than the son's.
